title: Skims Advent Calendar Refunds Amid Viral Backlash
summary: Skims faced backlash over a $148 advent calendar of keychains and hair ties. The brand offered refunds and credit after viral criticism.

 Our take
 Skims’ rapid refund offer demonstrates the brand’s responsiveness to consumer backlash, potentially preserving its image amid a high‑profile controversy. The underwhelming contents of the calendar highlight the risk of marketing strategies that rely on hype rather than product value.
 Background
 Skims is a lingerie and loungewear brand founded by Kim Kardashian in 2019 that offers shapewear, underwear, and apparel.
 In November 2026, Skims released a $148 accessory advent calendar that quickly faced backlash after a viral TikTok video highlighted its contents of keychains, ornaments, hair ties, and other small items.
 The timeline
 Nov 9, 2026 
 Skims Offers Refunds and Credit After Backlash
 Skims reportedly issued a statement to USA TODAY offering full refunds or credit to customers who purchased the advent calendar. [1] 
 Nov 10, 2026 
 Skims Responds to Backlash via Page Six
 Skims spokesperson reportedly admitted the advent calendar did not meet expectations and offered refunds or credit to customers. [1] 
 Nov 10, 2026 
 Skims Removes Calendar Listing After Backlash
 Skims reportedly removed the advent calendar listing from its website following consumer criticism. [1] 
 Our read of the evidence
 Mostly unverified. All three timeline events rest solely on reporting from dexerto.com with no primary source confirmation. No statements from the brand or other parties are documented as on-the-record in the available evidence. The claims remain unverified pending independent corroboration.
 Our rating counts evidence, not opinions about anyone: events confirmed by a primary source (the person's own post, their official site, a court or government record) weigh most, then how many independent outlets report the story.

 Skims issued refunds because the calendar did not meet customer expectations, as stated in their public apology.

 The calendar contained keychains, ornaments, hair ties, and other small accessories.
 Did Kim Kardashian comment on the controversy?
 Kim Kardashian has not weighed in on the controversy herself.
 Will the advent calendar be restocked?
 There is no mention of a restock following the backlash.

Kim Kardashian’s Skims responds to backlash over viral $150 advent calendar full of “junk”
 by Connor Bennett 
 Published: Nov 10, 2026, 10:56 
 Save for later

 Add as a preferred source on Google Follow on Google News 
 Kim Kardashian’s Skims has responded to the backlash about their $150 advent calendar, as one viral TikTok highlighted what’s inside, and some viewers said it was full of “junk.”
 With Christmas not too far away, plenty of people have already started looking towards the holiday season. That means buying presents, finding a tree to decorate, and getting an advent calendar. 
 However, when it comes to the latter part, Kim Kardashian’s Skims has been taking some flak. The underwear brand released an advent calendar of accessories for $148, but it was quickly ripped apart on TikTok . 
 One TikToker’s video, which has 68 million views , called it “way too expensive,” after she found the advent calendar full of keychains, ornaments, hair ties, and other small accessories. The TikToker even said that the final window had to be “made of gold” to make it worth their while. 
 Skims responds to viral backlash over $150 advent calendar
 Speaking to Page Six, a Skims spokesperson said they have “listened carefully” to the backlash and admitted that the advent calendar “didn’t meet expectations” for fans.
 “We want every customer to be truly happy with what they receive from Skims,” they continued. “Their feedback matters to us and will directly shape how we approach future releases.”
 Additionally, they noted that Skims has “personally contacted every customer who purchased the calendar and offered them a choice of a full refund or a Skims credit to put towards other products.”
 Reddit The contents of the Skims advent calendar 
 Some social media users have pointed out that a description for the advent calendar does list what is behind each window.

 Another described it as a “box full of pranks,” while another called it “genuinely disrespectful to customers” as they believe the items are only worth “$20 at best.”
 As it stands, the advent calendar is listed as being sold out on the Skims website, but there are no mentions of whether or not it will be restocked following the drama.

Kim Kardashian forced to issue refunds after SKIMS $148 advent calendar backlash 
 The internet’s complaints were heard loud and clear.
 By Samantha Olson Published: 10 November 2026 
 Save Article 
 %0A%09<path d="M240,128a15.74,15.74,0,0,1-7.6,13.51L88.32,229.65a16,16,0,0,1-16.2.3A15.86,15.86,0,0,1,64,216.13V39.87a15.86,15.86,0,0,1,8.12-13.82,16,16,0,0,1,16.2.3L232.4,114.49A15.74,15.74,0,0,1,240,128Z">%0A</path></svg>" width="60" height="60" alt="Play video"/> 
 'Tis the season for over-the-top advent calendars, and everyone from H&M to Dior is offering 12 (or 24) days of holiday fun for a pretty penny. Kim Kardashian’s fan-favourite brand, SKIMS, is also taking part in the shoppiest time of the year. However, customers who dropped their hard-earned cash on the SKIMS advent calendar are anything but pleased after receiving a bunch of keychains, scrunchie sets, and… bra straps/headbands?
 Fans called Kim and her brand out for the quality of products featured in the calendar, which was advertised as an “accessory advent calendar” and retailed for $148.
 “Kim Kardashian is really out here charging $150 USD for a SKIMS advent calendar and THIS is what you get??! bitch what if i was bald???” one person wrote , while another joked that its contents were “basically the stuff that fell down the side of the seat in my car.”
 They’re not entirely wrong. Unfortunately, it’s giving that one photo of the “sandwiches” at Fyre Festival... IYKYK.
 View full post on Instagram 
 They even started issuing full refunds, per email screenshots provided by customers who bought the calendar.
 According to a video shared by content creator and pop culture investigator Sloan Hooks , the company issued emails to customers offering full refunds or store credit.
 “We wanted to reach out personally about your recent purchase of the Holiday 2026 advent calendar. We understand the product did not meet customers’ expectations, and we are truly sorry. We want every customer to be happy with what they receive, and we fell short this time,” the customer service email read, in part, before suggesting solutions.
 “Let us know which option you’d prefer, and we’ll take care of the rest. Thank you for being our customer, and again, we apologise for the disappointment,” they continued.
 View full post on Instagram 
 After screenshots of the email started surfacing, SKIMS released a statement to Today , saying, “We have personally contacted every customer who purchased the calendar and offered them a choice of a full refund or a SKIMS credit to put towards other products. We want every customer to be truly happy with what they receive from SKIMS. Their feedback matters to us and will directly shape how we approach future releases.”
 Kim has yet to weigh in on the controversy herself, but SKIMS seemingly removed the listing from its website after receiving backlash for its selection of products.
 From: Cosmopolitan US
